rounds.text: Sanjivani Parenteral Ltd carries a valuation and fundamental trajectory that the current evidence does not support, underscored by a contracting trailing twelve-month profit growth of -8% [E15] paired with sluggish sales growth of only 4% [E14]. Despite this stagnant-to-negative operational reality, the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 32.2x [E1] (or 35.13x against a sector benchmark of 31.86x) [E6] and an aggressive price-to-book ratio of 4.99x [E2] (4.87x versus a sector benchmark of 2.96x) [E7]. This expensive multiple is further detached from reality because recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 1%, indicating that investor expectations are running dangerously ahead of actual financial delivery [E49], leading to a 1-year share price contraction of -7% [E19]. Conceded: the company exhibits a higher ROA of 7.62% compared to the sector benchmark of 5.63% [E8], and strong historical medium-term share price growth [E17, E18]. However, these historical gains and minor efficiency advantages do not justify paying a severe premium for a business whose current annual profits are shrinking [E15] while sector peers grow at a median profit rate of 19.0% [E64] and sales rate of 17.3% [E65].
